bearings.paper_claim: PCA of the 60 raw items gave six components (Big Five plus acquiescence) in both samples. Within-person centering removed the sixth. The five centered components had primary loadings averaging .62 (internet) and .61 (student), with congruence .97 or higher. The 15 facet scales gave five components above the scree line (eigenvalues 4.05, 2.16, 1.90, 1.60, 1.32, then 0.56 or lower). Averaging raw unreversed items gives an acquiescence index from 1.00 to 5.00.
bearings.paper_location: Study 3 domain-level structure pp. 30-31 (Table 6, Table 7, Figure 1); General Discussion p. 45
bearings.system_side: big5_llm.py docstring line 7 says balanced keying. The ITEMS table has 3 true-keyed and 1 false-keyed item for O, C, E and A (negatives at lines 59, 63, 67, 71) and 2 and 2 for ES (lines 74-75). The keyed mean is at line 344. Under an all-yes response the four 3:1 traits score +0.5 and ES scores 0.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The acquiescence mechanism carries over only if the LLM shows a +1 tendency on observer items, which is untested. Under the paper's logic a yea-saying tendency lifts O, C, E and A together and leaves ES alone, so it would not create the A-ES correlation by itself. The paper's content balancing controls acquiescence at the scale level, not at the item level.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers and page locations verified. The code keying and the docstring-versus-table mismatch are real. Not verified: the CT-CM MISS verdict and the A-ES halo of about .21 were not found in the repo files searched; big5_ctcm.py contains only the bar logic and branch text. The claim that content-balanced facets never produce acquiescence overstates the paper, which says they effectively control it in the facet PCA only (p. 31) and that acquiescence still biases same-domain facet associations (p. 33).

bearings.paper_claim: The BFI-2 has 15 facets, three per domain. E: Sociability, Assertiveness, Energy Level. A: Compassion, Respectfulness, Trust. C: Organization, Productiveness, Responsibility. N: Anxiety, Depression, Emotional Volatility. O: Intellectual Curiosity, Creative Imagination, Aesthetic Sensitivity. Domain scales have 12 balanced-keyed items; the 60-item form and scoring key are in the Appendix.
bearings.paper_location: Study 1 Phase 1 pp. 15-18; Table 1 p. 61; Appendix pp. 78-79
bearings.system_side: b5_panel_items.py holds 15 observer items, three per domain, with REVERSED = E1, A2, C1, C3, N3, O2 (C has two reversed items; E, A, N and O have one each). PROVISIONAL_TEXT is False at line 9, with a note that the wording was verified verbatim against the companion short-form paper. trait_score takes keyed means with no acquiescence correction.
bearings.code_ref: fec/members/b5_panel_items.py:3-9 (header and PROVISIONAL_TEXT); b5_panel_items.py ITEMS and REVERSED; b5_panel_items.py trait_score
bearings.transfer_conditions: This paper does not contain the BFI-2-XS item set. The one-item-per-facet fact and the verbatim check come from the companion short-form paper (Soto and John 2017, JRP), which is not in this item. Three items per domain cannot give facet scores or balanced keying, so the acquiescence results here transfer to the XS panel only weakly. The panel is CANCELED per the memory index, so this bearing is lineage only.
bearings.verifier_note: Facet names and the three-per-domain structure verified against this paper. Keying counts verified against REVERSED. The verbatim-verification claim rests on the code note alone and was not checked against the XS paper. The original bearing attributed the one-item-per-facet XS fact to this paper, which is wrong.

bearings.paper_claim: Self-peer domain agreement ranged .42 to .69 (mean .56) and facet agreement .27 to .73 (mean .49) in the student sample, with 184 peers (60 percent friends, 30 percent romantic partners). Cross-instrument convergence of the BFI-2 with other Big Five measures runs .72 to .92, from NEO PI-R to BFI.
bearings.paper_location: Study 3 self-peer agreement p. 29 and Table 4 p. 64; convergence pp. 34-35 and Table 9 p. 70 (N = 438 student sample)
bearings.system_side: fit_smoreg_rkh.py fits SMOreg-type weights to the RKH per-member targets and reports 5-fold held-out Pearson r. The ACTIVE weights are read from liwc/mairesse_smoreg.json (line 56). The docstring carries caveats on persona transfer. The bearing's held-out values (E .510, A .406, C .363, ES .258, O .214, mean .350) were not found in the script or in fec/liwc.

bearings.transfer_conditions: Use the paper's figures only as a rough scale for convergence and self-peer agreement, not as a bar. The paper compares human self-report with human peer report, and its convergence figures come from the student sample. The shared-method claim (Mairesse and LIWC on both sides) is not stated in the script and is not confirmed here.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers verified. The sample qualifier for convergence (student, N = 438) is missing from the bearing text. The system-side CV figures could not be located and need a source file or a rerun before they are cited.

bearings.paper_claim: Negative Emotionality facets predict different criteria. Peer-rated stress resistance is predicted by Emotional Volatility (r -.47, beta -.32) and Anxiety (r -.46, beta -.28); positive relations by Depression (r -.53, beta -.38). Facets average R2 .33 against .27 for domains across 20 criteria, and BFI-2 facets add significant variance over BFI domains for 14 of 20 criteria. Predictive utility depends more on facet quality than on facet count.
bearings.paper_location: Table 10 p. 71; Nomological network pp. 36-39; footnote 7 p. 39; Table 11 p. 72; General Discussion p. 44
bearings.system_side: emit_affective_n.py line 45 sums the four LLM facets (pessimism, anxiety, depression, volatility). Lines 52-56 E-residualize that sum and control for party. Line 42 and line 59 say LIWC is only the convergent-validity anchor and no longer a component, so the affective N is not combined with a LIWC read. The docstring at lines 3-4 still says it combines LIWC and is stale. receptivity_layer.py lines 176-189 feed the N slot into susc_trait at weight .30, and a code comment marks the affective option as the round-7 default.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The pressure mechanism fits Anxiety and Volatility more closely than Depression or pessimism. Keeping those components apart is a later measurement question that would need its own prereg and look. Transfer is weak because the paper's criteria are general-population self-report and peer ratings, not legislators' decisions. The genre-transfer rho values and the H5 null were not checked here.
bearings.verifier_note: Table 10 values, the R2 means and the 14 of 20 incremental count all verified. The bearing's statement that the affective N is combined with a LIWC-style read is wrong for the current code path, which is E-residualized and party-controlled LLM output only. The genre-transfer and H5 claims are unverified.

related.why: Translates the BFI-2-XS, the extra-short form derived from this paper's 60-item BFI-2, into 39 languages. Title confirmed; the XS derivation is not stated in this paper.
Expert ratings of U.S. senators' traits, the kind of other-rater criterion whose convergence the BFI-2 self-peer figures help calibrate. Title confirmed.
Speech-based Big Five estimates for elite members, the approach the lexical reader follows. The BFI-2 adds hierarchical facets and self-report benchmarks. Title confirmed.
Meta-analysis of LIWC and Big Five correlations, which brackets the text-to-trait convergence reachable against self-report. Title confirmed.

Pressure-choking study whose composite the receptivity N weight follows (the code comment cites Byrne et al.). Title confirmed; the BFI-2 facet results bear on which N component carries that mechanism.

summary_issues: The sentence saying content-balanced facet scales never produce acquiescence overstates the paper. The paper says they effectively control it in the facet PCA (p. 31), but it also says acquiescence still biases same-domain facet associations (p. 33).
The convergence range of .72 to .92 comes from the student sample (N = 438, pp. 34-35); the summary leaves out that qualifier.
The expert panel sentence says the BFI-2-XS takes one item per BFI-2 facet. That fact comes from the companion short-form paper, not from this JPSP BFI-2 paper.

The affective-N statement that the read is combined with a LIWC-style read is wrong for the current code. emit_affective_n.py lines 42 and 59 make LIWC an anchor only; the docstring at lines 3-4 is stale.
The held-out CV figures (E .510, A .406, C .363, ES .258, O .214, mean .350) are not found in fit_smoreg_rkh.py or fec/liwc. Cite a source file or rerun before use.
The A-ES halo of about .21 and the CT-CM MISS verdict are not found in the repo files searched; big5_ctcm.py contains only the bar logic and branch text.

The paul_alignment claims about Paul's notes are unsupported: paul_entries is empty and no markup was supplied. The Ramey and Birkenmaier and Lechner basis and the 10 personalities quote cannot be checked from this item.
